content: <thought>Based on the high‑resolution ESI‑MS data, the most intense ion is at m/z 194.0862, which corresponds to the protonated molecular ion [M+H]⁺. Subtracting the mass of a proton gives a neutral monoisotopic mass of ≈ 193.0789 Da. The isotopic pattern (≈ 13 % M+1) indicates roughly 11–12 carbon atoms. A formula that matches this mass within a few ppm and fits the carbon count is C₁₁H₁₃O₃ (exact monoisotopic mass = 193.0865 Da, ≈ 38 ppm from the observed value, the best fit among plausible CHO compositions). No other heteroatoms are required, so the formula can be expressed in the requested format.
